reference_reader: dissect.etl 3.14 (AGPL-3.0-or-later), external Python validation process; not linked or copied into application
notes: ETL reading performed on Linux by independent dissect.etl, not Windows OpenTrace.
EventHeader provider GUID is exported from raw ProviderId bytes with UUID(bytes_le=...), since dissect.etl EventHeader.provider_id currently displays first GUID components using wrong endianness.
replay_flags infer 32/64 and classic bits from on-disk header kind/marker. These are not native OpenTrace normalization results.
EventTraceHeader Version field is packed Type/Level/Version; exporter decomposes it explicitly.
Disk ETL order is buffer order, not the timestamp order delivered by native ProcessTrace.
Reference timestamp strings are dissect calculations and not independently verified UTC anchors.
Large source archive net.4.5.x64.etl.zip contains net.4.5.x86.etl, while session pointer size is 8 and some event headers are 32-bit.
PerfView baseline text may truncate long values and is corroboration rather than a complete machine-readable oracle.

primitive-types.etl TraceLogging metadata declares both int64_type and uint64_type as UInt64 (raw type byte 10 at extension-data offsets 123 and 136). PerfView's baseline renders the former as negative Int64; do not infer signedness from that field name or baseline text. TraceEvent 4.0.0 DynamicTraceEventData.PayloadFetch collapses TDH UInt64 to System.Int64.
